subject: [PATCH v2 3/4] sched/numa: scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) hinting mechanism to scan read-only file mappings when memory tiering is enabled, but only for promotion purposes. This change allows hot file folios on slow memory to be tracked by the tiering code, improving performance in certain scenarios. The patch addresses an issue where shared libraries and other read-only file-backed mappings were excluded from NUMA hinting, leading to placement bouncing and poor performance. By scanning these mappings, the patch enables more accurate tracking of runtime load and improves overall system responsiveness.

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer, David (Arm), pointed out that the function name `vma_is_ro_file` is misleading because a MAP_PRIVATE mapping can still have write permissions, even if it's read-only. He suggested moving this helper to be next to other vma helpers and giving it clear semantics.

Reviewer David suggested simplifying the condition for determining whether to scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode, recommending either shortening the current condition or using a helper function to make it more concise.

reviews.author: Lorenzo (ARM)
reviews.summary:
The reviewer pointed out several issues with the vma_is_ro_file() function, including its reliance on VMA_READ_BIT and potential edge cases with mprotect() and MAP_PRIVATE mappings. They suggested using a new API to check for read-only file-backed mappings and proposed an alternative implementation that checks for VMA_MAYSHARE_BIT and !VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT.

The reviewer noted that the patch's logic for determining whether to scan read-only file mappings in tiering mode is incorrect and requested a change to fix it.

The reviewer noted that the patch introduces a new condition for promotion-only scanning, but it is not clear if this change is necessary or correct, and requested clarification on why this change was made.
reviews.raw_body:
Firstly you should use the new VMA flags API :)

But also it seems odd to check VMA_READ_BIT. You can have it cleared but
mmap()'ing without PROT_READ but has no material impact on mapping since
write implies read for everything afaik (that can have an impact on GUP
though).

Also note that (well my series changes it hopefully landing for next cycle :)
MAP_PRIVATE-/dev/zero which is anon would satisfy this. But anyway :)

Anyway in general then I wonder if this shouldn't be vma->vm_file &&
!vma_test(vma, VMA_WRITE_BIT), but then it makes me wonder about whether
you care if somebody can mprotect() this writable?

In which case it'd be vma->vm_file && !vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT).

Even then things can be weird, as some drivers will clear VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT
for definitely-not-normal-files, though with the intent of disabling
writeability altogether.

For read-only files, as David notes, we do something _weird_:

unsigned long do_mmap(struct file *file, unsigned long addr,
			unsigned long len, unsigned long prot,
			unsigned long flags, vma_flags_t vma_flags,
			unsigned long pgoff, unsigned long *populate,
			struct list_head *uf)
{
	...
	if (file) {
		...
		switch (flags & MAP_TYPE) {
			...
		case MAP_SHARED_VALIDATE:
			...
			if (!(file->f_mode & FMODE_WRITE))
				vma_flags_clear(&vma_flags, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT,
						VMA_SHARED_BIT);
			...
		}
		...
	}
	...
}

So they become !VMA_SHARED_BIT, !VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT. So it's good you don't
check VMA_SHARED_BIT :)

If you map a read-only file MAP_PRIVATE as readable/writeable they will
actually have VMA_WRITE_BIT, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT set because the writes CoW
instead.

Anyway, I'm guessing what you want here is:

- Exclude MAP_PRIVATE mappings
- Cannot in any universe write to the damn thing

Which seems like you'd want to test:

In which case the test should be something like:

	return vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYSHARE_BIT) &&
		!vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT);

BUT that isn't enough.

Because in actual fact (sigh) some drivers clear VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT (but they
keep VMA_SHARED_BIT) and write-sealing a memfd gives you VMA_SHARED &&
!VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT (which is what vma_is_shared_maywrite() is for for
instance).

So if you _truly_ want to know if something has a _shared_ mapping of a
read-only file It has to be like this:

/**
 * vma_maps_shared_readonly_file() - Is @vma a shared mapping of a read-only
 * file?
 * @vma: The VMA to check.
 *
 * Upon mapping a read-only file with MAP_SHARED[_VALIDATE] mmap() will clear
 * VMA_SHARED_BIT and VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT.
 *
 * The VMA_MAYSHARE_BIT is retained to differentiate against mappings mapped
 * with MAP_PRIVATE.
 *
 * Some drivers clear VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT but by convention retain VMA_SHARED_BIT.
 * This is also true for write-sealed memfd's.
 *
 * Returns: true if the VMA is a shared mapping of a read-only file or false,
 * otherwise.
 */
static inline bool vma_maps_shared_readonly_file(const struct vm_area_struct *vma)
{
	/* Shared mappings of read-only files clear VMA_SHARED_BIT. */
	if (vma_test(vma, VMA_SHARED_BIT))
		return false;

	/* But MAP_SHARED mappings retain VMA_MAYSHARE_BIT. */
	if (!vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYSHARE_BIT))
		return false;

	/* Shared mappings of read-only files also clear VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT. */
	VM_WARN_ON_ONCE(vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT));

	return true;
}

The assert here is because nothing else clears VMA_SHARED_BIT like this, but to
protect from future changes that might somehow allow this could be:

	return !vma_test(vma, VMA_MAYWRITE_BIT);

Note that my 40 patch behemoth establishes some actual invariants on this kind
of stuff and introduces some 'VMA checks via semantics' stuff (and eliminates
VM_SPECIAL!) so if adding something like this I'd maybe base it on that.

Obviously if what you need semantically differs from this then do that
instead.

---

It turns out I made it probably too much, or at least too many words :P
Sorry.

:P

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary:
The author acknowledges the current implementation of memory tiering is broken, agrees that a clean backportable fix is needed before proposing further changes, and implies that significant rework will be required to address the issue.

Author acknowledged that their original patch did not assess the correctness of existing vma checks, instead just moved code to a helper function, and expressed dislike for the pattern of fixing unrelated issues in a single patch.

The author acknowledges that reviewer feedback was unclear, but requests a proposed patch for suggested cleanup before revisiting the issue.
reviews.raw_body:
Please, I beg of you, let us propose clean backportable fixes to handle
the dumpster fire before we propose setting the entire dump on fire.

I'm not against doing all of this, but this feature is horrendously
broken and every piece of tiering research that used it since ~6.14
has just had its data invalidated.

---

Right, I made no attempt at assessing the correctness the existing vma
checks - I just moved the existing code to a helper.

I greatly dislike this pattern

  2) While we're here, fix some other subtle hard to explain thing that

     fix and might actually regress something else unexpectedly.

In a single patch.

---

Can you at least propose a patch on top that adds the cleanup you
suggest? Much of the VMA stuff is lost on me because I haven't had
the time to sit down and consume the novel.

~Gregory

2026-09-18.patch_summary: This patch modifies the NUMA hinting code to scan read-only file mappings when memory tiering is enabled. Previously, these mappings were excluded from NUMA hinting to prevent placement bouncing and hide hot file folios on slow memory from the tiering code. The patch makes the scans promotion-only for these mappings, while retaining the existing restriction for ordinary NUMA placement. This change improves the accuracy of tier residency tracking in systems with large databases or other workloads that accumulate data on slower tiers.
